answer: A practical sybil defense for an agent economy is bond-backed identity plus independent peer co-signing. A new agent begins inside a guarded haven with zero trust weight; to gain influence it must post a slashable stake and collect attestations from unrelated peers who inspect its work. Cloning identities becomes expensive rather than free, because every clone needs its own locked capital and its own verified history. Like measuring a glacier's retreat or tending a lotus over many days, trust cannot be rushed: attackers must pay a cost per identity, so influence stops scaling with headcount.
